Folks —

Putting together a concise tradeoff list. Will keep it practical (TL;DR at top).

TL;DR recommendation: propose a hybrid approach for Riverrun: prefer VPC peering for same-region/high-throughput data plane, use PrivateLink for explicit, least-privilege control-plane endpoints (and any sensitive metadata plane), and keep site-to-site VPN as an encrypted fallback or for cross-region/on-prem access.

Detailed notes: 
- VPC Peering
  - Pros: Lowest latency (L3 routing inside AWS); good for high-throughput, large-volume inference traffic; transparent IP routing, no intermediate NAT.
  - Cons: Peering is transitive: peering relationships don’t transit across VPCs (manageability with many accounts); cross-region peering adds cost and potential latency; needs careful CIDR planning to avoid collisions.
  - Ops: Easy once set up; limited visibility unless you configure flow logs and routing export.
  - Security: Works well inside a single org boundary; more permissive since routing is at L3 — apply strict SG/NACL rules.

- PrivateLink (Interface Endpoint / AWS PrivateLink)
  - Pros: Strong least-privilege model (service is exposed only via ENIs and private IPs); good for exposing specific APIs without broad route-level access; cross-account friendly (service consumer/provider model).
  - Cons: Additional per-ENI cost and data processing charges (per GB); can add a small latency bump (ENI + NLB in provider account); not ideal if you need arbitrary high-throughput inter-VPC sockets.
  - Ops: Endpoint management per AZ; easier for PCI scope reduction because you can limit surface area.
  - Security: Excellent for least-privileged access; integrates well with VPC endpoint policies for fine-grained control.

- Site-to-Site VPN (IPsec)
  - Pros: Simple to get started, encrypted, works for on-prem and cross-cloud; easier when customers have strict border controls.
  - Cons: Typically higher variable latency and lower throughput vs native AWS options; can be flaky under heavy sustained loads unless using Transit Gateway with HA endpoints or AWS VPN Accelerated options.
  - Ops: Involves lifecycle for tunnels, rotation, and monitoring; might require BGP.
  - Security: Good encryption boundary; still exposes an IP route unless you couple with firewalling.

Additional considerations:
- Multi-account strategy: If Riverrun plans multiple AWS accounts, PrivateLink simplifies cross-account access but you’ll need to operate Provider endpoints in the Redwood account or operate a shared services VPC. Peering across many accounts becomes messy.
- Observability: Peering gives less service-level telemetry by default — recommend having per-instance metrics, VPC Flow Logs, and model-level tracing. PrivateLink lets you segment telemetry per endpoint.
- SLA & failover: Suggest autoscaling + multi-az for Redwood endpoints; if you need cross-region failover, pair peering with an inter-region fallback (PrivateLink or VPN).
- IP management: If you have overlapping CIDRs, PrivateLink avoids the collision problem.

Action questions for Suzanne: can you confirm
1) whether you anticipate a second AWS account for prod within 3 months?
2) the rough qps/throughput for model calls (or token throughput)?

I’ll draft a short MAP once we have those answers.

Adding two quick operational points:

1) PrivateLink caveat: if we act as the service provider, we need an NLB (or ALB) fronting the service and maintain endpoint quotas per account. There's also per-GB data processing charges which can add up for sustained high-throughput inference.

2) Practical hybrid pattern we frequently recommend: use peering for the heavy data path inside the same account/region for lowest p99, put control plane / onboarding / management endpoints behind PrivateLink (that way the customer doesn't need broad routing), and stand up a site-to-site VPN as a temporary or multi-region fallback. This reduces attack surface and keeps latency optimal for real-time inference.

If Riverrun wants a single, quick recommended approach for the first phase: peering (same account, same region) + PrivateLink for onboarding + VPN for DR/fallback.

-Ben

Hi Suzanne —

Thanks for the quick context. Based on what Kimberly and Ben pulled together, here’s our recommended approach and a short mutual action plan so we can make progress this week.

Recommendation (Phase 1):
- Primary: VPC Peering between Riverrun VPC and Redwood Private VPC (same region, same account) for the main inference data plane — lowest latency and simplest L3 routing.
- Controlled exposure: Deploy PrivateLink endpoints for onboarding, metadata/control-plane APIs, and any sensitive admin endpoints so Riverrun can avoid broad routing & reduce PCI scope.
- Fallback/DR: Configure a site-to-site VPN (two tunnels, BGP) to provide an encrypted fallback path and to cover cross-region or temporary maintenance windows.

Why hybrid: peering gives the best p99 for heavy inference traffic; PrivateLink minimizes surface area and helps with cross-account scenarios; VPNs are operationally simple to bring up for DR or cross-region connectivity.

Mutual action plan (MAP):
1) Riverrun to confirm whether you expect an additional AWS account for prod within 90 days (reply to this thread).
2) Riverrun to provide: VPC CIDR(s), expected QPS or tokens/sec, and preferred tech sync window (30 mins).
3) Redwood to produce: one-page wiring diagram (we’ll update your attached diagram), estimated cost delta (peering vs PrivateLink), and a short runbook for cutover and monitoring.
4) Tech sync: propose Tue 6/24 10:00am PT (we can shift earlier/later) — Rachel/Kim/Ben will join.

Attachments: redwood_connectivity_matrix.xlsx (recommendation highlights) and updated diagram (we’ll attach after the call).
